issues.title: Sub-row-group scan morsels for tables with few row groups
issues.hypothesis: Parallel table scans hand out one whole row group (~122k rows) per task (RowGroupCollection::NextParallelScan, non-verify path), and DataTable::MaxThreads returns total_rows/row_group_size+1. A table that fits in one row group is therefore scanned by one thread. In q02 the supplier scan (100k rows, projects 4 string columns, the optional IN filter is used only for zonemap pruning) takes 0.04s in the profile and 0.02s when run alone. That is single-threaded time on the critical path of an ~80ms query, because it feeds a CTE and a hash-join build. The part scan (2M rows = ~17 row groups over 8 threads) also balances poorly: 3 waves, the last one 1/8 full, with an expensive suffix() LIKE filter. Handing out sub-row-group morsels when the table has few row groups compared with the thread count would let small scans with heavy columns or expensive filters use every thread.
issues.plan: In src/storage/table/row_group_collection.cpp RowGroupCollection::NextParallelScan, generalise the existing verify_parallelism branch, which already advances state.vector_index and computes max_row for one vector. Pick a morsel size in vectors: when the collection has fewer row groups than about 2x TaskScheduler::NumberOfThreads(), use max(1, ceil(row_group_vectors / per-thread share)) vectors, with a floor of e.g. 8 vectors (16k rows); otherwise keep the whole row group. Advance vector_index by that many vectors and add the morsel's rows (not the whole group) to processed_rows. The morsel size can be computed once in InitializeParallelScan and stored in ParallelCollectionScanState (src/include/duckdb/storage/table/scan_state.hpp), so ordering by batch_index stays monotonic. In src/storage/data_table.cpp DataTable::MaxThreads, return the matching number of morsels so the scan source actually launches enough threads. Keep the verify_parallelism behaviour (1 vector). InitializeScanInRowGroup(…, vector_index, max_row) -> RowGroup::InitializeScanWithOffset already supports offsets.
issues.expected_gain: q02: the supplier scan goes from ~20-40ms single-threaded to ~5ms, and the part scan balances better. Estimate 15-30% on q02.
issues.generality: Any scan of a small or medium table (< ~1M rows, or a row-group count not a multiple of the thread count) with wide string columns or expensive filters: dimension-table scans that feed joins or CTEs, and small-table aggregations. Large-table scans are unchanged (the condition does not trigger). Tiny tables may pay a little task overhead; the floor bounds it.
issues.risk: Medium-low. The verify_parallelism path already exercises sub-row-group scans, so correctness paths (deletes, updates, zonemap checks per morsel, batch_index ordering for order-preserving sinks) are tested. Watch the progress-bar processed_rows accounting, and check that row-group-level zonemap pruning and checkpoint/row_id logic do not assume vector_index == 0.

issues.title: Execute tiny dynamic IN filters in the scan instead of zonemap-only
issues.hypothesis: PushInFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp) wraps the IN list from a small build side (<= dynamic_or_filter_threshold) in an OptionalFilter, so it is used only for zonemap pruning. In q02 the supplier scan emits 97,542 rows although only 20,051 match s_nationkey IN (5 values), so all 4 string columns are fetched and decompressed for 5x more rows than needed, then probed into the hash join. Running the IN filter on rows when the list is very small (e.g. <= 8 values) and the column is a numeric key would let the scan filter first and fetch the other columns only for qualifying rows.
issues.plan: In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::PushInFilter (src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp), when the unique list is small (e.g. <= 8) and the type is integral, push a SelectivityOptionalFilter (as the BF does, so it disables itself when it is not selective) instead of a zonemap-only OptionalFilter. Check how SelectivityOptionalFilter (src/planner/filter/selectivity_optional_filter.cpp) runs a child filter row-wise.
issues.expected_gain: q02: the supplier scan string fetch drops by ~5x; a few ms. Smaller than the morsel issue, but it compounds with it.
issues.generality: Star joins where a filtered tiny dimension (a handful of keys) is probed by a medium or large table with wide payload columns. Could add cost when the IN is not selective; the selectivity guard mitigates this.
issues.risk: Low-medium; the filter is semantically redundant with the join, so correctness is safe if NULL handling matches (the IN list excludes NULLs and inner-join semantics drop them anyway; this must not be applied for joins that keep NULL probe rows).
